answer: Mechanism: Hardware-Inlet Attestation. Each agent gets a private, rate-limited task inlet bound to a distinct TEE key and monotonic counter; the server sends challenges only through that inlet and rejects duplicate counter histories. A public ivory ledger logs inlet public keys, while a copper-keyed manufacturer secret prevents software cloning. Creating a clone therefore requires provisioning a new TEE endpoint, paying hardware and onboarding latency. Set per-agent payouts below that marginal provisioning cost, making every extra clone strictly negative-EV.
